description: Issue summary: Beacon Health reports that scheduled cohort alerts tied to a monthly window (30–90 day ranges) stopped triggering after a retention compaction job ran on 2026-03-09. Impact: multiple missed SLO alerts and missing tracehook links in alert digests. Environment: prod (us-east) console and scheduled export pipeline. Urgency: customer has enterprise SLOs tied to these alerts — requires investigation and mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer scheduled cohort query: org=beacon, cohort=monthly_active_users, window=30d-90d
Confirm scheduled alert config in Console > Scheduled Alerts > Beacon Health > monthly_cohort_alert
Wait for scheduled run at 03:00 UTC (daily digest), observe alert did not fire and exported digest has empty tracehook links
Run ad-hoc cohort query from Console for same time range (30–90d) — query returns data and trace links are present when executed manually
logs_and_evidence: Customer-provided digest: digest-2026-03-10-03:00.json (attached) — alert section empty and tracehook fields null
Console scheduler logs: scheduler/us-east/compact-run-2026-03-09.log shows retention compaction completed at 2026-03-09T02:18:43Z
Alerting service logs: alert-eval/us-east/2026-03-10T03:01:12Z WARN 'no series matched after rollup'
Grafana panel: scheduled-job-latency spike during compaction window (link provided by customer)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: compaction and rollup jobs run during the customer's scheduled window. Hypothesis: compaction moved high-cardinality route identifiers into archive tier before scheduled alert eval which uses the rollup index, causing sample-filtering to drop cohort series.

Checked scheduler ordering: retention compaction finished at 02:18Z, next scheduled alert eval queued at 03:00Z — sufficient gap, but backfill/reshard job triggered at 02:55Z per logs and may have altered partition ownership.

Queried backend index: found that route_id namespace for org=beacon was compacted and assigned to cold partition with different indexing keys (prefix-truncation applied). This changes tracehook token join key used by scheduled digest export.

Reproduced in staging: ran compaction + scheduled alert run on a copy of Beacon's data; scheduled alert did not match series when rollup index had compaction-truncated keys. Manual ad-hoc query used raw event store and succeeded.
comments: Customer (Elena @ Beacon): We missed three outbound SLO alerts yesterday morning. Can you confirm whether data was deleted or just inaccessible to scheduled alerts?
Support (Maya): Thanks Elena — investigating. Can you attach the scheduled digest you received? Also sharing scheduler and alert logs with engineering. #support
SRE (Luca): Observed retention compaction at 2026-03-09T02:18Z. Noted a reshard job at 02:55Z that likely changed partition mapping. Pushing to eng to validate index-key invariants.

Eng (Arjun): Reproduced locally in staging. Root cause appears to be prefix-truncation applied during compaction which is not compatible with the scheduled-alert join logic that expects full route_id keys. Preparing patch to fallback to raw-key join when scheduled-eval detects compacted-rollup state. See PR linked.
Customer (Elena): Appreciate the quick follow-up. Need ETA for workaround; our compliance team expects notification for missed alerts.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-12T09:40Z): scheduled-alert-worker updated to detect 'compacted-rollup' flag and use raw-event fallback join for the next 48 hours for orgs with high-cardinality cohorts. This restored alerts for Beacon on subsequent runs.
Code fix merged to staging: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2294 introduces defensive join behavior and additional telemetry when rollup key normalization is present.
Customer notified: Support sent customer-facing summary and offered a one-time audit of other scheduled alerts that overlap with compaction windows.
follow_up_actions: Engineering to harden rollup-key compatibility: add migration/compatibility shim to production rollouts (owner: Arjun, due 2026-03-20)
SRE to schedule compaction/reshard windows to avoid peak scheduled-alert times for enterprise customers in us-east (owner: Luca, actioned 2026-03-13)
Product to document recommended guardrails for customers with long-range cohort queries and plan a UX note in scheduling page (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-25)
Support to follow up with Beacon Health on remediation summary and offer 1:1 review (owner: Maya, follow-up 2026-03-14)
